::: {.tut-standfirst}
Step-by-step guides to take your occurrence spreadsheet from the field notebook to a Darwin Core Archive, following the same workflow as the application, step by step.
:::

The tutorials follow Saíra's workflow, step by step. Use the **sidebar** on the left to move between them and the **previous / next** buttons at the bottom of each page: the reading flows continuously, from installation to the final export. Each step can also be read on its own.

## The workflow, from raw data to DwC-A

1. **[Installation and first steps](01-installation.qmd)**: install Saíra from GitHub and open the application in your browser.
2. **[Importing your data](02-upload.qmd)**: load CSV or Excel spreadsheets (or a camera-trap package) and run a first inspection of the columns.
3. **[Mapping fields to Darwin Core](03-dwc-mapping.qmd)**: match each column to a Darwin Core term with automatic suggestions, templates and the `basisOfRecord` assistant.
4. **[Validating scientific names](04-name-validation.qmd)**: check nomenclature against Flora do Brasil, Fauna do Brasil or GBIF, resolve synonyms, correct names and see which taxa are threatened per the national MMA list.
5. **[Validating coordinates](05-coordinate-validation.qmd)**: find missing, swapped or transposed coordinates, fill the country from the point and review on the map.
6. **[Generalizing sensitive species](06-generalization.qmd)**: decide, species by species, whether and how much to reduce coordinate precision for threatened taxa, following Chapman's (2020) decision table.
7. **[Preview and export](07-preview-export.qmd)**: review the result and the corrections and generate the Darwin Core Archive.

::: {.callout-note}
## The workflow is flexible
You do not have to follow every step in a rigid sequence. Saíra lets you go back to any step (remap a field, reload the spreadsheet or revalidate) without losing the work already done. You can move backward at any time.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Practice with the sample file
Download the sample spreadsheet [`ocorrencias-exemplo.csv`](../../assets/exemplo/ocorrencias-exemplo.csv) and follow the tutorials with it. It is a deliberately imperfect sample dataset (several columns to map, one swapped coordinate and a blank country to fix during validation).
:::
